clue.text: Top-class villain in farewell theatrical performance

indicators.note: in says the top-class letter and the villain sit inside the word for farewell

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
U is the old British label for upper-class, top-drawer
the Devil is the arch-villain

explanation.surface: A first-rate baddie appears in someone's farewell stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old shorthand for upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U usage; the Latin farewell is split to take the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaudeville is a variety show of songs and sketches, a kind of stage entertainment.

clue.text: Patch up part of shoe

definitions.meaning: to repair or refurbish something old
the upper front part of a shoe

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a makeshift repair and the front upper of footwear.

clue.text: Ignoring the odds, turned boy loose

indicators.note: ignoring the odds says letters one, three, five and so on are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Disregarding the chances, the lad was let go.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'turned boy' are U, N, D, O.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot is to unfasten it.

clue.text: Point when that older you appears twice as attractive

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
as can mean when
yon is an old word for that
thee is an archaic form of you, and so is ye: the phrase appears twice
thee is an archaic form of you, and so is ye: the phrase appears twice

explanation.surface: There's a moment when an aged person looks doubly appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears twice' says 'older you' is used for two pieces: THEE and YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy on the eye is an idiom for good-looking.

clue.text: Valuable commodity — gold-found in plant

indicators.note: found in says the gold letters sit inside the plant word

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A precious trade good, gold, is discovered growing in a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant tusk material was a prized article of trade.

clue.text: Law-breaker defended by non-professional brief

indicators.note: defended by means guarded on both sides, so the lawbreaker sits within the other word

parts.note: laical means lay, not of the clergy or a profession
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: A criminal is represented by an amateur legal brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a lawyer's brief in this courtroom picture; it is the definition, meaning terse.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconical is an old form of laconic, terse in speech.

clue.text: Moslem. I rule to some extent

definitions.text: Moslem. I rule to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says only part of the following words is used, a run hidden across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of Moslem through I into the start of rule

explanation.surface: A Muslim speaker claims a partial authority.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'extent' as the definition, but no four-letter run here means extent; 'to some extent' is the whole hiding signal, and the clue as a whole is the ruler speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim prince or commander governing a state can say exactly this of himself.

clue.text: Easy, for example, involving MD in mishap

indicators.note: involving in its old sense of entangling or rolling together says the letters after it are mixed up

explanation.surface: A doctor gets caught up in an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's novel; MDINMISHAP rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marryat's Jack Easy is a junior naval officer, a cadet of that rank.

clue.text: Cock gun covering a policeman once

indicators.note: covering says the gun word wraps around the a

parts.note: rod is slang for a gun
the Bow Street Runners were an early London police force

explanation.surface: Someone cocks a gun while hiding an old-time constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cock' looks like a verb about the gun; it is the bird, the roadrunner also being called the chaparral cock.
explanation.definitionFit: The American desert cuckoo is also known as the chaparral cock.

clue.text: Money-making ability possibly said to get involved in a good deal

indicators.note: get involved in places the rearranged letters within the word for a good deal

parts.note: much means a good deal

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of said to are to be taken in some other order

explanation.surface: A knack for making money might be said to come from getting into a big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns SAIDTO into IDASTO, which goes into MUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phrygian king of legend turned all he touched to gold, so his touch is the gift of easy wealth.

clue.text: I had streamlined each plan

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
ea is the shortened, abbreviated form of each

explanation.surface: Someone simplified each scheme they had.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or scheme in the mind is a plan of action.

clue.text: Most ceased work before union meeting in connexion with building

indicators.note: most says nearly all of the word is used, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: struck means went on strike, ceased work
TU is short for trade union
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Most workers walked out ahead of a union gathering about construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ceased work' means went on strike; 'Most' drops its last letter, and 'before' simply sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Structurally means with regard to the way something is constructed.

clue.text: Hare, perhaps, is drab — the cony's different

definitions.note: William Hare, of Burke and Hare, supplied corpses to Edinburgh anatomists

indicators.note: different says the letters of the three words that precede it are made into something else

explanation.surface: A hare is dull-coloured, unlike the rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Hare looks like the animal beside the cony (an old word for rabbit), but it is the 1820s Edinburgh murderer who sold bodies for dissection.
explanation.definitionFit: Burke and Hare killed people to sell their corpses, the trade of grave-robbers who sold cadavers to medical schools.

clue.text: Professed love within reasonable time

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: within says the time letter goes inside the word for reasonable

parts.note: sensible means reasonable

explanation.surface: Someone declared their love within a fair period.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as love, with time in reasonable: O, then T inside SENSIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent or declared, as in a professed rather than real motive.

clue.text: Prosthesis that feels, at first, ever so strange

indicators.note: so strange says the letters are put into an odd new order
at first takes the opening letter of ever

explanation.surface: A false body part feels very odd at first.
explanation.walkthrough: THATFEELS plus E, the first letter of ever, rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are an artificial replacement for natural teeth, a prosthetic device.

clue.text: Wise guy, in other words, about to spoil story

indicators.note: about says the abbreviation for in other words goes around the rest

parts.note: sc, short for Latin scilicet, means namely, that is, in other words
mar means spoil
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A smart guy, put differently, is set to ruin the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: SC, for Latin scilicet, is the dictionary abbreviation meaning namely; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a know-all, the sarcastic sense of a wise guy.

clue.text: Poet has to chase after Aurora

indicators.note: after says the word for chase follows the name that goes with Aurora

parts.note: Aurora Leigh is the verse novel by Elizabeth Barrett Browning
to hunt is to chase

explanation.surface: A poet has to pursue a dawn goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Aurora is not the dawn goddess but the heroine of Barrett Browning's poem, whose surname follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: James Henry Leigh Hunt was an English Romantic writer of verse and essays.

clue.text: A foreign method of identification is loose

parts.note: un is a in French, a foreign word
a PIN, personal identification number, identifies a card holder

explanation.surface: A foreign ID system is unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose something is to unfasten it, as when taking out a fastening pin.

clue.text: Result in forming a unit without it

indicators.note: without says the word it is removed from the phrase meaning forming a unit

parts.note: en suite, French for in a set, describes rooms forming a single unit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that forms a unit leaves 'it' out.
explanation.walkthrough: EN SUITE (as a hotel bathroom attached to its bedroom) loses IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a consequence is to result.

clue.text: Unable to relax, I will worry about beginning to age

indicators.note: about says the words for I will worry go around the first letter of age

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
to tease is to worry or pester

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the opening letter of age

explanation.surface: Someone who can't unwind frets about getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' applies to the whole of 'I will worry', which wraps the A from 'beginning to age'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ill at ease means feeling uncomfortable and tense, not relaxed.

clue.text: They're beasts, disposed to kick up a dust

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of the two words before are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Animals are inclined to stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: THEYREBEASTS rearranges into the twelve letters; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To set people by the ears is to stir up quarrels between them, causing a commotion.

clue.text: Little boy that's climbing high mountain

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue says the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Reg is a short form of the boy's name Reginald
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A small lad is scaling a lofty peak.
explanation.walkthrough: REG plus IE read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiger is a famous Alpine peak in Switzerland.

clue.text: Flower — surreptitiously remove head

indicators.note: remove head says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: slily, a spelling of slyly, means surreptitiously

explanation.surface: A gardener secretly beheads a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The lily is a bulb plant with large trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Old and grey — every day starting thus

indicators.note: starting says each word gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: Elderly and grey: every day begins that way.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'and grey every day' spell the answer; 'thus' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, having lived long.

clue.text: Generated sound money

indicators.note: sound says the word for money is heard rather than written

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Created a healthy financial position.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means produced offspring, brought into being.

clue.text: Glued pieces broken, caught by stick in beating

indicators.note: caught by says the rearranged letters are held inside the word for stick

parts.note: to cling is to stick

indicators.note: pieces broken says the word glued is smashed and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Glued fragments come apart when hit with a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like the weapon in this scene but is the verb, cling; 'pieces broken' makes UDGEL, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cudgelling is hitting with a club, a beating.

clue.text: Narcissus didn't want her parrot

definitions.meaning: the nymph who pined for Narcissus, who loved only his reflection, until only her voice was left
to parrot is to repeat what another says

explanation.definitionFit: The rejected nymph faded to a repeating voice, and to repeat another's words is to parrot them.

clue.text: Idealistic, stopped consuming rum initially, then whisky

indicators.note: consuming says the word for stopped swallows the following letters

parts.note: stayed means stopped

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of rum

parts.note: rye is a whisky distilled from rye grain

explanation.surface: A dreamer stopped drinking rum first, then whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' keeps the rum's letter ahead of the whisky inside the word for stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry-eyed means naively romantic, full of unrealistic hopes.
